sections.title: Annual nettle
sections.text: Urtica urens is an annual nettle, usually about 60 cm tall and up to roughly 75 cm. It has stinging hairs and toothed leaves; unlike the common perennial nettle, its leaf base is usually not heart-shaped. The plate’s compact, toothed plant and small flowers fit.

sections.title: Sting and food use
sections.text: Its hairs cause the characteristic nettle sting. Kew records this species as used for food, and young leaves are described as edible after cooking; raw contact can still irritate, so handling and eating are different concerns.
